protocol.source_fit: One XGBoost model per source database and landmark on all source patients with a mapped outcome who reached that landmark.
protocol.model_reuse: The same source-landmark model is transported to both target databases; no target information enters fitting.
protocol.target_evaluation: All target patients with a mapped outcome who reached the same landmark.
protocol.transition_alignment: Exact target IDs in the complete 24/48/72 h cohort. Weights are fixed within each independent source-landmark model; 24 h and 72 h weights are not shared, so temporal change also includes model refitting.

recalibration_protocol.target_probability_source: Fixed source-model predictions on each target patient; target outcomes are never used to fit the transported XGBoost model.
recalibration_protocol.calibration_features: Both methods use natural logarithms of the three transported class probabilities clipped to [1e-8, 1].

calibrators.multinomial_logistic: sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression with multinomial three-class targets, C=1e6, lbfgs, max_iter=5000, tol=1e-8.
calibrators.temperature_scaling: One positive class-independent temperature fitted by bounded scalar minimisation of calibration-set log loss.

recalibration_protocol.calibrator_comparison: Both calibrators are fitted on the same deterministic splits. Paired differences are descriptive and were not selected by direction-specific performance.
recalibration_protocol.sampling: One target stay is retained per patient before repeated outcome-stratified sampling without replacement, with at least one patient from each class. Independent class permutations use a SHA-256 seed derived from the global seed, direction, landmark, and repeat.
recalibration_protocol.evaluation: Recalibrated predictions for target patients not selected into the local calibration subset; calibration and evaluation patients are disjoint.
recalibration_protocol.n_zero: Untouched transported predictions on the same one-stay-per-patient target population; no split is used because no local labels are consumed.
recalibration_protocol.interval: 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles over deterministic repeated target splits.

interpretation_boundary: MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-III are same-institution, cross-era databases; their transport directions are not independent external validation.
Fixed-weight transport is retrospective and not prospective deployment.
Target recalibration estimates data requirements for calibration, not clinical utility, process improvement, or patient benefit.
Facility is a heterogeneous administrative destination and does not form a verified continuous severity scale with home and death.
